claims.text: Adding 0.1–0.5 at% boron to a refractory HEA will improve its high-temperature creep resistance.
The boron addition will enhance grain-boundary cohesion.
Boron preferentially segregates to grain boundaries in the refractory HEA.
Boron segregation strengthens bonds at grain boundaries and reduces grain-boundary mobility.
Enhanced grain-boundary cohesion inhibits grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
Enhanced grain-boundary cohesion inhibits diffusion-controlled creep mechanisms at elevated temperature.
Suppressing grain-boundary mobility, sliding, and diffusion-controlled mechanisms retards high-temperature creep deformation.
A boron concentration of 0.1–0.5 at% is low enough to avoid formation of detrimental brittle phases.
The low boron concentration will preserve room-temperature ductility.
The boron addition will not significantly increase the alloy density.
At approximately 1000°C under sustained load, the boron-added alloy will exhibit roughly 20–30% greater creep strength than the boron-free baseline.
The boron-added alloy will retain tensile strength comparable to that of the boron-free baseline at room temperature.
The boron-added alloy will retain ductility comparable to that of the boron-free baseline at room temperature.
The expected benefit depends on boron remaining finely and uniformly distributed at grain boundaries without precipitating as brittle borides or other deleterious phases.
Exceeding boron solubility limits or unfavorable segregation kinetics may cause local embrittlement.
